The upper bound condition is: Md≤1.5 Ze fyγm0M_d \leq 1.5\, Z_e\, \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}Md​≤1.5Ze​γm0​fy​​

Explanation:
Zefyγm0Z_e \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}Ze​γm0​fy​​ is the elastic moment capacity (moment at which extreme fibre just yields).
The plastic moment capacity is Zpfyγm0Z_p \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}Zp​γm0​fy​​ where Zp=1.5 ZeZ_p = 1.5\, Z_eZp​=1.5Ze​ for a rectangular section (shape factor = 1.5).

The upper bound 1.5 Zefyγm01.5\, Z_e \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}1.5Ze​γm0​fy​​ equals the full plastic moment capacity.

The reason for capping at 1.5Ze1.5 Z_e1.5Ze​ is to ensure that plastic deformation does not occur under working (service) loads. If the design moment exceeds this limit, the section would undergo plastic deformation at service load level (with appropriate load factors), causing permanent deformation.

Therefore, The upper bound prevents plastic deformation under working load.
